title: Recursive Superintelligence signs $410 compute deal with Amazon
summary: Recursive’s $400 million outlay represents the bulk of the company’s fundraising to date.
full_text:
On Tuesday, the AI company Recursive Superintelligence announced a $400 million compute deal with Amazon Web Services. The company, which emerged from stealth in May with $650 million in funding, is focused on building open-ended self-improving systems, a potentially compute-intensive approach to AI research. This multi-year deal is meant to provide flexibility as the company looks to scale up those systems.
Recursive’s $410 million outlay represents the bulk of the company’s fundraising to date— but on a call with TechCrunch, Socher emphasized that he expected it to be the first of many such deals. Today’s announcement is “likely going to be one of the smallest compute deals we’re going to sign in the next few years,” Socher said.
Recursive’s emphasis on self-improving AI systems means much of the budget that would traditionally go towards headcount and operations is put straight into compute, as the company seeks to automate its own product development process.
“For us, it’s less about headcount and more about agent count,” Socher said.
There’s no investment component to Amazon’s involvement, in contrast to major labs’ habit of hybrid investment arrangements. But the sheer scale of the commitment allows AWS to commit significant resources to supporting Recursive’s unique needs, which may help to draw in other foundation-level AI companies going forward.
“Part of the agreement is that we’re going to co-develop infrastructure purpose-built for these types of company,” said Jason Bennett, VP for startups and venture capital at AWS.
Recursive self-improvement (RSI) has long been seen as an inflection point for AI, with some expecting an explosion of progress once AI can be improved without human involvement. But as more labs and companies pursue the idea, the specific requirements have become ambiguous, with some predicting an imminent breakthrough while others characterize self-improvement as more of a continuum.
But in Recursive’s case, the goal is to use the powers of RSI to develop actual products — and Socher expects to be releasing the earliest examples before the end of the year.
“We are excited to build like really amazing products that people can use, and you will see those within a few months, not within a few quarters or years,” Socher says. “In October or so, you’ll see some actually tangible, useful things that you’ll be able to play around with.”

title: Granola launches an Apple Watch app
summary: Granola debutes an Apple Watch app for in-person notetaking
full_text:
AI note-taking app Granola is launching an app for the Apple Watch in hopes that its users will want to record meetings and take notes without using their smartphones.
Users can set the Granola app as one of the watch faces to start transcribing at any time. The app can also surface reminders about upcoming meetings, and works with the iOS app, which launched last year.
The company’s co-founder, Chris Pedregal, told TechCrunch that the Apple Watch app is meant to be a way to capture in-person meetings without having to take your phone out of your pocket — for example, if someone is having a walking one-on-one meeting.
When Granola tested its app with employees who had Apple Watches, a big chunk of their mobile usage switched from iOS to the Watch, the company said.
In the past year, companies have released auxiliary devices that can be used with smartphones to record and transcribe meetings. Granola said it considered it easier to develop an app for Apple Watches rather than integrate with another hardware product at this point. Dictation app Monlogue earlier this year also added support for meeting note-taking, for both online and offline modalities, along with Apple Watch support.
Granola became a unicorn earlier this year with a $125 million Series C round that was led by Index Ventures.

title: As US measles cases rise, biotech firms start developing new treatments
summary: The US is making measles great again, so treatment options are needed for the most vulnerable.
full_text:
Up until recently, measles vaccination has been so effective that there’s been little medical or financial incentive to develop treatments for the disease.
But as measles cases hit a 35-year high and vaccination rates continue to decline in the US, a handful of biotech companies and academic groups have started working on measles treatments for those infected with the virus as well as vulnerable individuals needing short-term protection. It will likely be years, however, before these countermeasures are available, and it’s even more uncertain if those who refuse vaccines would take such treatments.
Fueled by large outbreaks in South Carolina and Utah, the US had already surpassed last year’s 2,289 measles cases, and it’s only July. For comparison, there were just 285 cases in all of 2024.
Because measles is so contagious, at least 95 percent of people in a community need to receive both doses of the measles vaccine to protect immunocompromised individuals and infants under 12 months old who are too young to be vaccinated. But measles vaccination rates have dipped well below that in many places across the country.
Young children are the most susceptible to severe complications from measles. The virus can cause pneumonia by damaging the respiratory tract lining directly and by suppressing the immune system, leaving them susceptible to bacterial infections. It can also cause deafness and potentially fatal brain damage. Without a measles-specific treatment, doctors rely on supportive care such as preventing dehydration, managing breathing difficulties, and administering steroids for inflammation. Vitamin A is sometimes given to patients because the virus can deplete levels of it in the body, but the supplement has no effect on the virus itself.
“What we’re seeing now as we get a resurgence of measles in communities is a horrible lack of options when somebody gets exposed,” says Michael Mina, an epidemiologist and chief medical officer of Invivyd, a Connecticut-based biotech company.

title: Is the Electric Trike the Next Big Thing in Shared Micromobility?
summary: Veo is launching accessibility-focused electric tricycles in Denver, with plans to put its e-trikes on the streets nationwide.
full_text:
Rideshare micromobility vehicles are a common sight in major cities around the world, whether that’s a bicycle program or electric scooters. Now, a company called Veo is introducing electric tricycles into the mix.
Announced Tuesday at an event in Denver, the company showed off the Rover, a three-wheeled, sit-down electric vehicle designed for anyone to ride on the streets. They are available in Denver for now, but Veo plans to expand the vehicle to cities across the US.
The Rover works like a shared bike or e-scooter. Sign up for the Veo app, pay a fee to unlock the trike, and then ride it around. It’s 2.5 feet wide, which means it can legally fit within bike lanes that are usually three feet wide. The trike has a max speed of 10 miles per hour. Cities tend to cap these kinds of rental bikes and scooters at 15 mph, but Veo chose to go with a slower speed for safety reasons. The Rover uses the same batteries as Veo’s other EV offerings, giving it a range of roughly 45 miles per charge; on the rear is a cargo basket that can hold up to 100 pounds of luggage or groceries.
Veo is a smaller player in the micromobility space, operating in about 60 smaller cities in the US. In May, the city of Denver signed an exclusive contract with Veo to replace the city’s scooters and ebikes made by rival companies Lime and Bird. Now the sole supplier of shared bikes and scooters in Denver, Veo wanted to use the city to show off the newest addition to its micromobility collection.
The Rover is primarily an accessibility play, as three-wheeled vehicles tend to stand on their own and self-balance better than two-wheeled bikes and scooters. City governments sometimes require micromobility companies to provide options for people who need more accessible vehicles. Lime has deployed a free accessible vehicle rental program called Lime Assist that lets users in need rent accessible vehicles for the day. Bird launched its own accessible rentals program in April. Veo offers similar options but wants to make those kinds of vehicles more widely available.
“The expectation is that your local bus or transit provider will offer accessible options for those who are in wheelchairs or can't use certain products,” Alexander Keating, Veo’s vice president of policy and partnerships, tells WIRED. “There's also an expectation for us, from the cities who permit our kinds of programs, to do everything they can to make them accessible.”
Veo says it worked with disability advocates, including the Disability Mobility Initiative, Parkinson's Foundation, and Capitol Hill Village, to design the Rover, along with organizations like the AARP to make something that would appeal to older users, too. The trike’s three-wheeled design means it is self-balancing, so people can hop on without dealing with it falling over or fiddling with a kickstand.
“Our goal is to make sure that no rider has to be treated differently in order to go through more barriers to enter the system,” Keating says.
Like Veo’s other vehicles, the Rover is equipped with an AI-powered voice assistant that can talk to the rider during a ride to share directions, location information, and traffic updates. The software also has other features like lidar sidewalk-detection tech that aims to keep people from bombing down sidewalks on their Veo scooters where they aren't allowed. (Denver locals have noted that the issue hasn’t exactly gone away since Veo took over.)
The software also collects geolocation and ride details from the person on the vehicle. Keating says this information is anonymized, but the company uses this ridership data to help get a handle on what kinds of trips people use them for as it makes plans to expand the trikes into other markets.
Electric bikes are very in right now, and companies like Lectric have already built electric tricycles. Trikes are more accessible for elderly riders, but they can also be heavier and more difficult to steer. How those factors play out and whether more people will want to try them is what Veo wants to figure out in Denver. Keating says, so far, he has been surprised by the response from people who have seen the Rover.
“We want people to think it's cool; that's what gets them on it,” Keating says. “You would think, like, trikes are for kids or trikes are for someone older. I think it might be for everyone. We're going to see.”

title: Best Gifts for Mom (2026): E-Readers, Digital Wall Calendar, Smart Bird Feeders
summary: Your mom never gets you a thoughtless gift, so you shouldn’t get her one, either. Here’s every cool gift WIRED writers would give their mothers.
full_text:
Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario. That includes Mother's Day, her birthday, Christmas, Hanukkah, or any other holiday in your family's life that includes gift-giving. I've made some additions for summer that are great for moms who have an upcoming birthday, or a mom you just want to treat with something nice for the warmest time of year.
If you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love. From wellness gadgets that can improve her skin, a beach bag I can't stop using, or even a device that puts her digital calendar in an IRL device, moms everywhere can get a ton out of these gifts. Many of these items I've given to my mother, or other WIRED staffers have given to theirs, or it's at the top of my list as a mother of a 4-year-old.
Updated July 2026: I've added a beach bag, sun hat, and linen-blend sheets as new gifts to this guide.
Featured Gifts
My Favorite Summer Bag
I've had this bag for a few summers now, and it's held up great. It's my go-to bag for the beach or pool, and the mesh sides make it breathable for sand and water alike. The slim straps have a ton of room to sling this bag over your shoulder or onto a wagon handle, and I haven't had any breakage even with all the towels, swimsuits, and more I stuff into it. The bottom is waterproof so it's perfect for sitting poolside, and the stylish colors make it a bag she'll love bringing. I prefer its look by a long mile to the bulky Bogg bags I spot at the pool, and it's better priced.
Next-Level Skin (and Scalp) Care
The must-have gadget for women of almost any age is an LED mask. These masks promise to use red light to erase wrinkles, brighten your skin, and keep acne at bay. I haven't seen much change in my wrinkles in my year-plus of regularly using a red light mask, but I can confirm it makes my skin brighter and calms down acne and scars much faster when I'm regularly treating my skin. HigherDose is a favorite mask of mine because the three-strap design lets it hang on my head rather than squeeze it, making it one of the most comfortable masks I've worn.
My other favorite LED tool actually sits on my head and also comes from HigherDose. The brand's Red Light Hat treats your head with red light to rejuvenate your scalp and hair follicles for better hair growth, and as someone with a sensitive scalp and a hair-pulling problem, using this cap regularly genuinely improved my scalp and hair. It's the healthiest it's ever been, and my scalp is the least itchy, too. I love that this hat also has a battery pack, so I can comfortably wear it anywhere while I treat my head.
Chic Sun Protection
I have managed to get two different scalp burns this summer, and I am seriously over it. My 4-year-old has me going everywhere from the beach to the pool to the county fair already this summer, and even sunscreen made for spraying into the crevices of my hair hasn't kept me safe. Enter: this Solbari wide-brim hat. It's soft and flexible, so it's easy to fold up and store in a beach bag or stroller, and the cotton-linen design keeps it pretty breathable, though you'll want to reverse it onto the white side for hotter days. It promises UPF 50+ to protect your head, and the 4-inch brim helps keep my neck safe, too. It's cute while still giving plenty of coverage, and a great pick for any mom who is going to be dragged into the sun all summer long.
Her Google Calendar IRL
My latest favorite family planning gadget is a digital wall calendar. These handy devices take the Google Calendar I live by (and just about any other digital calendar, if your mom isn't a Google girl) and put it on a physical device I can quickly tap into without needing to grab my phone or bark at Alexa. The Skylight Calendar 2 is my favorite, because it not only includes to-do lists, meal planning, and a recipe book but also doubles as a digital photo frame. That means it displays cute photos of my family most of the time, and then, with a simple tap, it opens the calendar or whatever page I was last on to show me what's on my family's schedule. It does have a subscription fee, though, to get the digital photo frame feature and a few other options, like meal planning. But I think it's well worth it to get so many features in a single device.
For the Reader
Look, I love a Kindle, but if you want to get the best e-reader for your buck, the answer is actually a Kobo. My favorite is the Kobo Libra Colour that's cheaper than the Kindle Colorsoft and can also double as a digital notebook if you add on the $70 stylus. I also prefer Kobo's annotating options: You can write right on the pages instead of in weird pop-up margins and boxes only on Kindle. Kobo also has its own page-turner remote now, which I love to pair with a pillow stand holder so I can lean back and relax without holding up my e-reader while I read. I gave a similar pillow stand to my mom, and now I can spot her last reading spot easily because that pillow is resting there.
Luxurious, Cooling Sheets
If your mom (or your wife) is complaining about the hot nights this summer, one of the best kinds of sheets to keep her cool is a set of linen sheets. These beautiful sheets from Modern Dane are made of 100 percent European flax linen that's grown in France, Belgium, and the Netherlands, and produced in Portugal. These sheets have a weight of 165 GSM, or grams per square meter, which is what linen sheets are graded on instead of thread count. That gives them a medium weight, but these sheets feel nice and light and have been perfect to sleep on during hot summer nights. Plus, these sheets are certified with OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Class 1 and Masters of Flax Fibre certifications. You can choose from a variety of colors and prints that will perfectly match her bedroom design.
Clear Listening
My husband and I got AirPods around the same time. We were late adopters and longtime fans of our Apple corded headphones. The AirPods 4 aren't the WIRED team's favorite for sound, but I'm one of the many people who can't seem to keep other earbuds in my ears, so Apple's tip-free design is the best fit for me, though that means you aren't getting good noise canceling. I got my first set for Christmas from my siblings this year, and originally I stuck some pretty stickers on my case to tell the difference between my case and my husband's. I've since upgraded to this stylish case from Mujjo, which makes it easy to see which is mine and clip it onto my keys. It's a nice accessory if your mom already has AirPods but struggles to keep track of them or is looking for an easier way to differentiate hers from the other members of the house.
Gamer Gear
Once my kiddo is asleep, you can find me parked on the couch with my Nintendo Switch. I recently upgraded to a Nintendo Switch 2 ($449) so I could finally buy and play Pokopia ($70), since it's exclusive to the new console, and I've already clocked an obscene amount of hours on the game. It's similar to Animal Crossing, but imagine it's all Pokémon instead of random animal people. It has a choke hold on me, similar to Animal Crossing: New Horizons did in 2020, and there have been multiple times when I'm still awake playing when my son has a midnight wake-up or an accident. (You could say it's helping me be ready to parent.) My son is 4 and not quite ready to really play a video game, but he does love to fly around as a Dragonite in this game, and he's loved watching the cutscenes with me when I complete parts of the story.

title: Best Apple Watch (2026): Series 11, SE 3, and Ultra 3
summary: Should you splurge on the new Series 11, or will the SE 3 do? Let us help you figure out which version to get (and which to avoid).
full_text:
The Best Apple Watch for Your Health, Fitness, and Everyday Life
Featured in this article
If you have an iPhone, the Apple Watch is the best wearable. It's the watch I'd wear if I weren't testing other fitness trackers. But what's the best Apple Watch to buy? With three models, each with unique attributes and features, this question has gotten harder to answer.
For the past few years, Apple has contended with a series of troublesome lawsuits and bans that led to the removal of its blood oxygen sensor (which is back). Last year, the company introduced a ton of new features, like satellite messaging and hypertension notifications. If you need help telling them apart, this guide breaks down what features are available on which watch, and whether older models are still worth the price. The latest operating system is watchOS 27, and I also discuss the Apple Watch's newest fitness-tracking features.
Be sure to check out our other related buying guides, including the Best Smartwatches, Best Fitness Trackers, and Best Sleep Trackers.
Updated July 2026: I've refreshed our recommendations, updated the specs, and revamped the product comparison table. I added sections for honorable mentions and frequently asked questions. Product information, prices, and links were also updated.
Honorable Mention
Apple Watch Series 10: The Series 10 features the same S10 chip found in all the latest Apple Watches. This was the first watch to feature a slim design and a wide-angle screen that fits nicely under your shirt sleeves. It has fast charging and is also compatible with watchOS 27 (with an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone). It doesn't have a 24-hour battery life, which makes sleep tracking tricky unless you prioritize wearing it overnight and go without it for much of the day. That said, it often goes on sale for significantly below the MSRP, so if you see it, it's worth snagging.
Compare Top 3 Apple Watches
Avoid These Watches
It's been years since we’ve seen retailers carry the Series 1, Series 2, or Series 3. You may see them on resale sites, but they're not worth the price. WatchOS 27 only works with the Series 9 and newer, so we no longer recommend buying the Series 4 or 5, or the second-gen SE. The Series 1 isn't waterproof, neither the Series 1 nor the Series 2 has any cellular capability, and none of these watches are compatible with the latest watchOS version.
Frequently Asked Questions
What Are the Fitness Features on the Apple Watch?
There are many reasons to wear an Apple Watch besides the health features. Maybe you just want quick access to your text, calendars, or Siri. Maybe you want to keep track of your kid or make sure your elderly mom doesn't fall down.
Still, I have been following the Apple Watch's development for years, from a fairly standard wearable accessory to a fully featured fitness tracker that now compares favorably against the high-end Garmins and Suuntos of the world. Since its inception, Apple has gone all in on the watch as a personal health device, with CEO Tim Cook even going as far as to say that the watch will save your life. Hypertension notifications and sleep tracking are a significant step forward, although the long-touted noninvasive continuous glucose monitor has yet to make an appearance.
In addition to health-related features, Apple has also unveiled additions to its workout programs over the past few months. The AI-enabled Workout Buddy in Fitness is perhaps the most prominent. Apple has also started offering Fitness+ in more countries and launching new workout programs, like three-week strength training programs that are designed to jump-start your workout routines.
Apple Watch data is compatible with many more fitness and workout apps besides Apple's proprietary Fitness+. For more information on which app is the right pick for your Apple Watch, check out our guide to the Best Fitness and Workout Apps. Fitness+ is also available on the iPhone, iPad, and Apple TV.
What Are the Best Apple Watch Apps and Accessories?
Once you have your Apple Watch, you're going to need some accessories. Here are the ones for you to consider first.
- A 3-in-1 charger. Apple Watches are notoriously hard to keep charged. This Belkin Qi2 charger ($110) is our favorite stand, but we have many more selections in our Best 3-in-1 Apple Wireless Chargers. You can also pick up a power bank ($90) with a built-in Apple Watch charger so you're not caught out and about with a dead watch.
- Whatever Apple Watch band you want. Our Best Apple Watch Accessories guide has a ton of options. My favorite band of all time is the Konsu NYC supple leather band ($185), but we have many more in our guide.
- A case and a screen protector. Apple's service pricing is notoriously exorbitant—repairing a watch costs almost as much as buying a new one! Bigger and more expensive isn't always better. If the case is big and doesn't fit well, it will rattle annoyingly every time you get a notification. I like the Spigen Thin Fit Case ($15) and a screen protector set from Amazon ($10); extras are nice if you mess up the first application.

12 Adventurous Gifts for Hikers, Backpackers, and Outdoorsy People

Buying gifts for the outdoor enthusiast is damn near impossible. Your hiking/camping/cycling outdoorsy friends are often serious gearheads, meticulously poring over reviews, guides, and the perennial wisdom of ounce-counting Reddit users to find the exact right thing.
Don't stress trying to pick that exact right thing yourself. The chances of you figuring it out and getting it for them as a gift is exactly zero. That doesn't mean you should punt and buy an REI gift card—although they might like that, especially with REI's annual Labor Day sale coming up. But gift cards are lame. Instead, get them something they totally didn't expect: one of these fun, useful, sometimes whimsical things that are almost guaranteed to not only delight them but actually get used outdoors.
And what about you? While you’re here, don’t you need to replace your sleeping pad? Don't forget to check out the rest of our buying guides, including our Best Sleeping Bags guide, our Best Barefoot Shoes guide, and our Best Merino Wool guide.
Updated July 2026: I’ve removed a few sold-out items and added a hat from Solbari and a nice leather journal. But I'm sticking with the socks as our top pick. If you get nothing else, just get the socks. Trust me.
- Merino Wool Socks- Darn Tough - Merino Socks- Yes, you read that right. Socks. SOCKS. You should gift socks. Outdoorsy people can never have too many socks. It’s also got a handy hole in the back for ponytails and braids, and the 5-inch brim in the front and 6-inch brim in the rear are longer than most hats of this style, to ensure you’re well-covered. It’s adjustable for different head sizes via a toggle in the back, and there’s a detachable chin strap, though for some reason this addition makes me feel like an elderly river-rafting guide, so I leave it off. (Though if it’s windy, it’s going back on—just call me Class Five Cloris.) —Kat Merck 
- Laws Guide to Nature Journaling- John Muir Laws - The Laws Guide to Nature Drawing and Journaling- This book changed the way I, and my kids, look at the world. I originally bought it because I thought my kids might like it (which they did), but then I stole it, read it cover to cover, bought a sketchbook, and, following along with the book, started to see the world in much more detail than I ever had before. Don't worry if your giftee is not an artist. I am the opposite of skilled when it comes to drawing, and I still love this book. More than drawing, what this book is teaching you is to look closely, observing and recording the world around you, and to form your own understanding of what you've witnessed. - If you want to put together a kind of “curiosity kit” gift package based on the one in the book, pick up a hand lens (I like this one because of the way it blocks out the light, though there are higher-quality lenses), some nice pens, and a millimeter ruler to go along with it. You could also check out our guide to journals and notebooks, though those tend to be very personal choices and might not be the best gift unless you know exactly what your giftee wants. 
- Coffee, Coffee Now- What is camping without brewing coffee over a morning fire? And what is coffee if not from a moka pot? This is the classic Bialetti moka pot on which all other moka pots are based. It's made of heavy-gauge aluminum that heats evenly and won't complain if you put it directly on the coals (although the plastic handle will, so make sure your outdoorsy person puts it on the edge of the fire). It'll brew about a 4-ounce cup of very dark coffee (not technically espresso since it's not under pressure, but it's as close as you'll get outdoors). - If your outdoor person isn't a moka pot lover, other coffee options include this exquisite titanium French press from Snow Peak. It weighs just 6.3 ounces, so you can even hit the trail with it if you’re dedicated to your coffee. Then there's the tried-and-true Aeropress Go ($50), which can be used in a variety of ways and is light enough to pack on the trail and simple enough to use in a hotel room—and it makes all-around good coffee. 
- A Tiny Wood Stove- Did you notice the photo of the moka pot above? That was on top of this stove. You would not think that a 3-inch folding metal box designed to efficiently burn twigs would inspire an almost religious devotion, and yet here we are. Firebox stoves come in a variety of shapes and sizes, but my favorite is the smallest, the Nano, which I've used for years as both a wood stove and a gas stove, even a grill (also an alcohol stove). It's my top pick stove for cooking in the backcountry, but that's not why I suggest you get it for your outdoorsy friend. There are plenty of stoves out there. Your outdoorsy friend probably has at least two very practical stoves. - No, the reason I suggest you get this for them is because outdoorsy people are practical, and they will never buy this for themselves because they don't get it. Yet. You will help them get it. This stove is fun. It's practical, too, but ignore that for now and focus on the fun. With the Firebox Nano you can build a small fire out of twigs and cook a steak on it. Who doesn't love that? It's an amazing thing to realize how little fuel it actually takes to cook something. Grill asparagus, shrimp, homemade tortillas.

title: 14.6 億用戶的未爆彈？調查：三分之二數位銀行無完整執照，AI 實際採用率僅 18%
summary:
數位銀行（Neobank）的繁榮榮景背後，恐暗藏驚人的結構性危機！據 Consensys 開發者關係負責人 F […]

〈14.6 億用戶的未爆彈？調查：三分之二數位銀行無完整執照，AI 實際採用率僅 18%〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
數位銀行（Neobank）的繁榮榮景背後，恐暗藏驚人的結構性危機！據 Consensys 開發者關係負責人 Francesco Andreoli 於 X 平台發布的最新萬字調查，全球 368 家活躍的數位銀行雖坐擁高達 14.6 億用戶，但竟有三分之二並未持有完整銀行執照。這種過度依賴底層 BaaS（銀行即服務）供應商的「租牌」模式，正成為下一個系統性未爆彈；此外，產業中真實將 AI 投入生產環境的比例僅有 18%。
（前情提要：俄羅斯最大銀行 Sberbank 12 月推加密交易基礎設施，數位託管庫先行）
（背景補充：英國國會啟動調查：加密公司被銀行擋在門外，FCA 授權 9 月底開放申請掃除障礙）
在金融科技與 Web3 浪潮的強力推動下，數位銀行（Neobank）正以前所未有的速度重塑全球金融版圖，讓許多人迎來了人生的第一次開戶。然而，台北時間 7 月 27 日，Consensys / MetaMask 開發者關係負責人 Francesco Andreoli 於 X（前 Twitter）發布了一份震撼業界的深度追蹤報告，無情揭露了這看似繁榮的表象背後，實則隱藏著極度脆弱的基礎設施風險。
亞洲稱霸市場，Web3 原生銀行強勢崛起
Andreoli 耗費大量心力追蹤並驗證了全球 368 家活躍的數位銀行。數據顯示，這些機構自行報告的用戶總數已高達 14.6 億人。在地理分布上，亞洲以 8.17 億用戶佔據絕對主導地位；單是中國的微眾銀行（WeBank）就服務了超過 4 億人，遠超歐美市場的總和。相比之下，歐洲的市場龍頭 Revolut 雖擁有逾 5,000 萬用戶，在亞洲巨頭面前仍顯得微不足道。
值得注意的是，在產業結構的演進中，加密貨幣與去中心化技術正扮演關鍵角色。報告指出，在 2020 年代成立且存活至今的數位銀行中，高達 30% 是「Web3 原生自託管」應用（共計 56 家），而這一比例在 2010 年代僅有 4%；此外，還有 58 家屬於混合法定貨幣與加密貨幣的應用程式。
致命弱點：三分之二無執照，淪為「租客」
這份調查最令人擔憂的發現，在於嚴峻的「執照缺口」。在追蹤的 368 家數位銀行中，僅有 127 家（約三分之一）持有完整的銀行執照。這意味著其餘三分之二皆是依賴贊助銀行（Sponsor bank）、電子貨幣執照或 BaaS 平台來「租用」牌照，而多數消費者對此毫不知情。
Andreoli 強調，這是整個產業的核心結構性風險。他列舉了過去血淋淋的崩潰案例：2018 年 Visa 撤銷 WaveCrest 發卡權，導致數十個加密卡專案一夜死亡；2020 年 Wirecard 爆發 19 億歐元漏洞，凍結歐洲多家新創銀行；以及 2024 年美國 BaaS 中間商 Synapse 崩潰，讓無數客戶驚覺自己的資金根本不受 FDIC（聯邦存款保險公司）保障。
當真正的銀行倒閉時，客戶有存款保險作為後盾；但當數位銀行的底層基礎設施倒閉時，客戶往往只能在破產程序中無助地排隊等候。Andreoli 形容這是一種「沉默的死亡」—— 光是本月就有 5 家機構悄悄清算或停止營運，幾十萬名客戶在沒有任何新聞稿的情況下被迫遷移或面臨資產消失。
AI 淪為行銷噱頭？全球南方才是實踐者
在人工智慧（AI）的採用上，報告也戳破了金融科技圈的過度包裝。經逐一審查，這 368 家機構中僅有 67 家（約 18%）真正在生產環境中部署了 AI 技術，其餘三百多家大多停留在試點階段，或是單純將合作夥伴的模型當作自己的行銷說辭。
有趣的是，真正領先將 AI 落地應用的，並非歐美大廠，而是位於奈及利亞、菲律賓、墨西哥與孟加拉等新興市場的放貸業者。由於當地缺乏完善的傳統信用局體系，依賴 AI 進行核貸成為這些業務得以生存的唯一理由。正如作者所言：「西方在『談』AI 銀行，而全球南方在『出貨』。」
未來三大預測：AI 核貸爆雷與「機器客戶」
基於龐大的數據分析，Andreoli 也對數位銀行產業提出了三大前瞻預測。首先，他認為「執照缺口」將從兩端收斂：強勢品牌將收購或取得自己的牌照，而弱勢品牌將在 2027 年前面臨淘汰，中間層將逐漸消失。
其次，他警告「第一波 AI 核貸爆雷」將在未來兩個信用週期內發生，因為目前這 67 個生產模型大多尚未經歷過真正的經濟衰退考驗。最後，他大膽預測「下一波客戶將不再是人類」，而是服務於 AI 代理（AI Agents）的銀行軌道——包含代理操作的錢包與機器對機器支付。這項趨勢目前僅有 7 家機構在探索，看似怪異，卻可能如同 2021 年的 Web3 原生應用一般，成為未來的結構性主流。

title: 1inch 推出自託管共享流動性層「1inch Aqua」：單一餘額支援多重部位、解決資金閒置痛點
summary:
據 1inch 官方部落格最新公告，1inch 於今（28）日正式推出名為「1inch Aqua」的自託管共享 […]

〈1inch 推出自託管共享流動性層「1inch Aqua」：單一餘額支援多重部位、解決資金閒置痛點〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據 1inch 官方部落格最新公告，1inch 於今（28）日正式推出名為「1inch Aqua」的自託管共享流動性層（Shared Liquidity Layer）。該協議主打讓用戶能用同一個錢包餘額，同時支援多個流動性部位，且代幣在實際發生交易前都不會離開用戶錢包，徹底解決了 DeFi 長期以來的資金閒置與 JIT 攻擊痛點。
（前情提要：1inch 共同創辦人宣布離職：去年11月就被辭退，帶 50% 股權啟動新計畫）
（背景補充：1inch投資人183萬美元賣單砸出7%跌幅！山寨幣流動性拉響警報）
在目前的去中心化金融（DeFi）生態中，流動性提供者（LP）往往面臨資金效率低下的困境。台北時間 7 月 28 日，知名 DEX 聚合器 1inch 團隊由 Vladimir Kozlov 發表最新文章，宣布正式上線「1inch Aqua」—— 這是一個旨在顛覆現有流動性玩法的自託管共享流動性層。
DeFi 流動性痛點：資金閒置與 JIT 攻擊
1inch 團隊在公告中直指當前 DeFi 流動性市場的核心痛點。首先，儘管許多流動性池擁有極高的總鎖定價值（TVL），但大部分代幣在多數時間內都處於閒置狀態，真正能發揮作用的流動性相當有限。此外，LP 必須將有限的資金分散投入到不同的協議、交易對與價格區間中，導致整體的資本利用率極度低落。
更嚴重的安全與收益問題在於「JIT（Just-in-Time）攻擊」。目前 LP 極易受到 MEV 機器人的針對，這些機器人會在大額交易發生前後，臨時插入並隨即撤出流動性，藉此搶走本應屬於長期 LP 的手續費，最高可能造成 LP 損失高達 44% 的費用收入。同時，傳統機制要求代幣存入智能合約，讓用戶喪失了對資產的絕對控制權。
Aqua 核心機制：代幣留存錢包，原子交易結算
為了解決上述問題，1inch Aqua 提出了「共享流動性（Shared Liquidity）」的全新解決方案。用戶只需將錢包連接至協議並批准特定代幣的餘額，即可自由創建多個流動性部位（包含全範圍、集中流動性或掛鉤型部位）。最突破性的設計在於，代幣從未被存入任何合約，而是始終保留在用戶的錢包中。
當市場上出現符合條件的交換訂單時，Aqua 協議會以原子交易（Atomic transaction）的方式，直接從用戶錢包提取所需代幣，並瞬間將兌換獲得的代幣與手續費推回錢包中。這種機制不僅讓同一個餘額能支援多個部位，更因為每個部位僅有單一擁有者，徹底阻斷了 JIT 機器人插入流動性搶奪手續費的可能性。
已支援 13 條 EVM 鏈，官方：DeFi 需要更有用的流動性
在安全性與可用性方面，1inch Aqua 強調所有交換均由已驗證的造市商或套利機器人執行，且實際風險暴露僅限於用戶錢包內的實際餘額（若餘額不足則不會調用），用戶亦可隨時無鎖定期地開啟或關閉部位。該協議已通過 Hexens、OpenZeppelin 等 8 個獨立安全團隊的嚴格審計。
自 2025 年 11 月向開發者開放測試後，1inch Aqua 如今已正式對所有用戶公開，並支援包含 Ethereum、Arbitrum、Base、BNB Chain 以及 Robinhood Chain 等 13 條 EVM 兼容鏈。1inch 官方在文末強調：「DeFi 不需要『更多』的流動性，而是需要『更有用、更風險可控』的流動性。」

title: 捨棄散戶轉攻機構！Luno 交易所裁員 20% 全球員工，加碼押注穩定幣基礎設施
summary:
加密貨幣市場持續低迷，促使交易平台加速戰略轉型。據《Bloomberg》最新報導，知名加密貨幣交易所 Luno […]

〈捨棄散戶轉攻機構！Luno 交易所裁員 20% 全球員工，加碼押注穩定幣基礎設施〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
加密貨幣市場持續低迷，促使交易平台加速戰略轉型。據《Bloomberg》最新報導，知名加密貨幣交易所 Luno 於今（28）日宣布，為因應零售交易疲軟並降低營運成本，將裁減約 20% 的全球員工。此次重組後，Luno 將把業務重心轉向利潤更穩定的機構服務、B2B 基礎設施，並計畫將其南非蘭特掛鉤的穩定幣模式擴展至更多新興市場。
（前情提要：被 AI 裁員的記者，發現公司還用自己名字發文章）
（背景補充：Uber 客服部門再砍 10%，承認裁員理由是擁抱 AI）
在經歷了市場週期的劇烈波動後，加密貨幣交易所正積極尋找更穩健的生存之道。台北時間 7 月 28 日，據《Bloomberg》引述 Luno 官方發布的最新消息，該加密貨幣交易所決定啟動大規模的組織重組，預計將削減約 20% 的全球人力。
零售疲軟促轉型，重心轉向 B2B 與合規
Luno 執行長 James Lanigan 在受訪時坦言，由於零售端的交易量持續呈現疲軟態勢，公司必須果斷降低成本以調整財務結構。他並未透露具體受影響的員工數量，但強調這項重組計畫將有助於公司全力擴展 B2B（企業對企業）業務。
Lanigan 進一步解釋，Luno 在過去一年中已投入大量資源進行自動化與提升營運效率，這使得業務運作所需的人員結構發生了快速且本質上的改變，因此目前迫切需要一個更精簡、重新調整的組織架構。未來，Luno 將把發展重心聚焦於三大領域：針對機構投資者的專業服務、核心基礎設施的建設，以及監管合規能力的強化；儘管如此，官方也承諾仍會持續投資現有的零售客戶產品。
瞄準新興市場，推動本地貨幣穩定幣
作為目前在非洲與亞太地區擁有約 1,600 萬龐大用戶群的交易所，Luno 早已開始為其轉型鋪路。近期，該公司積極擴展其 B2B 業務，為傳統銀行、金融科技公司與電信業者提供流動性、錢包與合規等底層基礎設施，讓這些機構能以自家品牌無縫提供加密貨幣服務。
此外，穩定幣戰略也是 Luno 未來發展的核心拼圖。作為與南非蘭特掛鉤的穩定幣「ZARU」創始參與者，Luno 計畫將這種成功的本地貨幣穩定幣模式，複製並推廣至其他極度缺乏此類基礎設施的新興市場。
《Bloomberg》分析指出，隨著散戶零售交易持續呈現高波動與不確定性，越來越多的加密交易所正如同 Luno 一樣，積極尋求來自機構客戶、B2B 支付與金融底層基礎設施等更為穩定且長期的收入來源，這已成為加密產業在市場低迷時期的普遍趨勢。

title: 亞馬遜 AI 策略大轉彎！逐步淘汰多數 Nova 旗艦模型，資源全押注「前沿模型」
summary:
面對生成式 AI 賽道的激烈競爭，科技巨頭亞馬遜（Amazon）正迎來重大的戰略轉向！據《Business I […]

〈亞馬遜 AI 策略大轉彎！逐步淘汰多數 Nova 旗艦模型，資源全押注「前沿模型」〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
面對生成式 AI 賽道的激烈競爭，科技巨頭亞馬遜（Amazon）正迎來重大的戰略轉向！據《Business Insider》報導，亞馬遜目前正大刀闊斧重整其 AI 策略，逐步淘汰多數自家開發的旗艦 Nova 模型，並將核心工程資源與算力全面集中於開發全新的「前沿模型（Frontier models）」。這項戰略轉變緊隨著近期 AGI 部門的裁員與高層人事重組，顯示亞馬遜正力圖以更聚焦的火力迎戰 OpenAI 與 Google 等強敵。
（前情提要：亞馬遜警告：記憶體危機將殺死遊戲主機與PC，雲端遊戲是唯一出路）
（背景補充：白毛股神 Serenity：OpenAI和亞馬遜的新網路架構「不會削弱光模組需求」）
在人工智慧軍備競賽進入深水區之際，亞馬遜（Amazon）決定重新調整步伐。台北時間 7 月 28 日，據《Business Insider》引述知情人士報導，亞馬遜正在全面且大幅度地重組其 AI 發展策略。
多數 Nova 模型進入「維持運作」狀態
這項轉變最顯著的動作，是亞馬遜已開始逐步淘汰多數自家開發的旗艦 Nova 模型。受影響的產品線包括高端的 Premier 與 Omni 模型、專注於影片生成的 Reel 模型，以及主打圖像生成的 Canvas 模型。
據部分內部員工透露，這些曾經被寄予厚望的模型目前已被降級至「KTLO（Keep The Lights On，維持運作）」狀態；這意味著公司雖然仍會為既有客戶提供基本支援，但已不再將其視為主要的開發與更新重點。不過，這並不代表亞馬遜將完全放棄 Nova 品牌，包含 Nova 2 Sonic、Nova 2 Lite 等基礎模型，以及 Nova Forge 和 AI 代理技術 Nova Act 仍會持續運作。
資源重兵集結，力推全新「前沿模型」
被騰出的龐大工程人才與稀缺的運算資源，目前正大幅轉向一個名為「前沿模型研究（Frontier Model Research，簡稱 FMR）」的新計畫。該計畫由透過收購 AI 機器人新創 Covariant 而加入亞馬遜的頂尖研究員 Pieter Abbeel 領軍。據悉，FMR 已躍升為亞馬遜今年度最優先的戰略項目，團隊正全力開發一款全新的旗艦基礎模型，並預計在今年秋季的 re:Invent 年度大會上正式亮相。
高層大洗牌，策略從「多方下注」轉為「高度聚焦」
這波策略大轉彎，與亞馬遜內部的人事大地震息息相關。回顧 2023 年，執行長 Andy Jassy 還親自支持 AGI 組織打造最雄心勃勃的基礎模型，當時團隊由長期負責 Alexa 的高管 Rohit Prasad 領導。然而，Prasad 已於 2025 年底離職，而專注長期研究、由 Adept 共同創辦人 David Luan 領導的 AGI Lab 也於上週正式關閉（Luan 本人於今年 2 月離職）。
目前，整個 AGI 組織已被併入資深副總裁 Peter DeSantis 旗下。在他的強勢主導下，亞馬遜的 AI 策略從過去「同時發展多種文字、圖像、影片模型」的多方下注模式，轉變為「高度聚焦少數前沿模型」的精兵策略。
對此，亞馬遜官方發言人回應表示：「AI 模型仍是我們最重要的工作之一，這一點沒有改變。就像任何 AI 產品組合一樣，我們會根據客戶需求持續調整模型陣容，並在模型升級時提供明確的指引與遷移路徑。」這場及時的戰略重組，是否能幫助亞馬遜在面對 OpenAI、Google 與 Anthropic 等強敵時扳回一城，市場正拭目以待。

title: 美國 SEC 主席表態：看好 Clarity Act 順利通關
summary:
據知名加密媒體 Bitcoin Magazine 於 X 平台發布的最新貼文，美國證券交易委員會（SEC）主席 […]

〈美國 SEC 主席表態：看好 Clarity Act 順利通關〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
據知名加密媒體 Bitcoin Magazine 於 X 平台發布的最新貼文，美國證券交易委員會（SEC）主席 Paul Atkins 在接受外媒《CNBC》專訪時，針對加密貨幣監管釋出了極為正面的友善訊號。他公開表態，對美國國會即將通過的加密監管法案《Clarity Act》抱持高度樂觀的態度，這番發言立刻引發加密社群熱烈討論。
（前情提要：美國參議院多數黨領袖：Clarity Act 恐趕不及 8 月前通過，兩黨分歧仍存）
（背景補充：川普鬆口放行「倫理條款」，加密法案 CLARITY Act 衝刺參議院表決）
台北時間 7 月 28 日，據 Bitcoin Magazine 於 X（前 Twitter）分享的一段 67 秒專訪影片顯示，現任 SEC 主席 Paul Atkins 登上了《CNBC》的新聞播報台，並對未來的 IPO 市場與加密監管法案發表了看法。
https://x.com/BitcoinMagazine/status/2082079240346886372
SEC 態度大反轉，盼法規建立明確框架
在採訪畫面中，Paul Atkins 面對鏡頭明確說道：「我樂觀地認為國會會通過 Clarity Act。」與此同時，新聞畫面下方的跑馬燈也同步顯示了一項重要資訊，指出該加密貨幣監管法案已於上週成功清除了「關鍵的倫理障礙（Key ethics hurdle）」。
這項簡短卻有力的發言，與過去數年來 SEC 模稜兩可的強硬執法態度形成了鮮明對比。市場普遍預期，《Clarity Act》若能順利立法，將為美國的數位資產市場提供一套透明、可依循的遊戲規則，大幅降低企業面臨的合規風險與不確定性。
社群嘲諷過往執法：這是最透明的發言
隨著這段專訪影片曝光，加密社群紛紛對 SEC 的態度轉變表達振奮與肯定。在該則貼文下方，有網友幽默地回顧了過去的監管困境，諷刺地稱這是 SEC 長期以來「最透明的發言」。
此外，也有不少用戶深刻認同法規清晰的重要性，並直言指出缺乏規則的「狂野西部模式行不通」。隨著 SEC 高層親自出面背書，接下來國會是否能如期推進《Clarity Act》的立法程序，將成為整體加密市場密切關注的重中之重。

title: 重懲豬仔園！緬甸通過《反線上詐騙法案》，涉「加密貨幣詐騙」最高處無期徒刑
summary:
為了打擊東南亞日益猖獗的「豬仔園」跨國詐騙產業，緬甸軍政府祭出了極度嚴厲的法律制裁。據《Decrypt》報導， […]

〈重懲豬仔園！緬甸通過《反線上詐騙法案》，涉「加密貨幣詐騙」最高處無期徒刑〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
為了打擊東南亞日益猖獗的「豬仔園」跨國詐騙產業，緬甸軍政府祭出了極度嚴厲的法律制裁。據《Decrypt》報導，緬甸議會於 7 月 28 日正式通過《反線上詐騙法案》，明訂對使用暴力強迫他人從事詐騙的犯罪份子最高可處以死刑。此外，針對在幕後經營詐騙中心或從事「加密貨幣詐騙」的主謀，最高將面臨無期徒刑的重罰。
（前情提要：東南亞詐騙園區末日？緬甸擬立新法：加密詐騙關到死，非法拘禁豬仔最重判死刑）
（背景補充：緬甸軍方誓言剷除 KK 詐騙園區，真的在做嗎或只是作秀？）
東南亞跨國詐騙集團的犯罪問題已引發全球高度關注，而作為詐騙園區大本營之一的緬甸，如今決定祭出重拳。台北時間 7 月 28 日，據《Decrypt》報導，緬甸軍方支持的議會於週二正式通過了《反線上詐騙法案》（Anti-Online Scam Bill）。
這是敏昂萊（Min Aung Hlaing）於 2026 年 4 月就任文職總統後，該國新政府所通過的第一部法律，強烈展現了當局試圖整頓日益擴張的網路犯罪產業的決心。
祭出死刑與無期徒刑！嚴打加密貨幣詐騙
這部新法案針對詐騙產業鏈的不同層級，制定了極具威嚇力的刑罰。根據規定，若犯罪份子使用暴力、酷刑、非法逮捕、拘留或殘忍手段強迫他人從事線上詐騙，最高可處以死刑；若相關惡劣行為導致受害者死亡，則法官「必須判處死刑」。
此外，針對在幕後經營線上詐騙中心，或是從事「數位貨幣詐騙（加密貨幣詐騙）」的主謀，最高將面臨無期徒刑；而強迫他人從事詐騙的相關罪行，刑期則落在 10 年至無期徒刑不等。緬甸下議院議員 Aye Chan 向媒體證實，死刑條款在法案最終通過的版本中得以保留，確保了該法案的重要部分維持不變。
詐騙園區年捲千億美元，成東南亞毒瘤
緬甸此舉主要針對近年在東南亞氾濫的強迫勞動詐騙園區。這些園區常以暴力手段，強迫來自全球至少 80 個國家的受害者從事愛情詐騙與加密貨幣投資詐騙。聯合國毒品和犯罪問題辦公室（UNODC）估計，僅在 2025 年，東亞、東南亞及大洋洲的詐騙活動就造成了高達 883 億至 1,141 億美元的驚人損失。
為應對此危機，各國已開始收緊執法網。除了柬埔寨近期也在推進針對詐騙首腦的終身監禁法案外，美國財政部更在 2025 年 5 月制裁了控制泰緬邊境詐騙溫床的克倫民族軍（Karen National Army），並查獲逾 2,500 萬美元與該地區相關的加密貨幣。聯合國也警告，該地區的執法單位目前仍難以有效追蹤複雜的鏈上資金流向。
死刑條款背後的政治角力
儘管打擊犯罪的立意明確，但這項嚴刑峻法的推行背景也充滿了濃厚的政治色彩。自 2021 年發動政變以來，敏昂萊政權於 2022 年首度恢復了司法處決，打破緬甸自 1976 年以來的禁忌。
有趣的是，敏昂萊在今年 4 月上任文職總統時，才剛宣布將全國所有的死刑減為無期徒刑；然而僅僅三個月後，由親軍方的聯邦鞏固與發展黨（USDP）掌控的多數議會，便迅速立法重新引入了新的死刑條款。這不僅被視為對跨國詐騙的強硬宣戰，也象徵著軍政府試圖藉此重塑其國內與國際威信的政治手段。

title: 鑽石手慌了？比特幣長期持有者交易所流入佔比飆破 5.1%，創 2020 年以來最高紀錄
summary:
加密貨幣市場持續震盪，鏈上數據揭露了比特幣長期持有者（LTH）的異常動向。據 CryptoQuant 認證分析 […]

〈鑽石手慌了？比特幣長期持有者交易所流入佔比飆破 5.1%，創 2020 年以來最高紀錄〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
加密貨幣市場持續震盪，鏈上數據揭露了比特幣長期持有者（LTH）的異常動向。據 CryptoQuant 認證分析師 Darkfost 於 X 平台發布的最新數據指出，近期 LTH 轉入交易所的資金比例高達 5.1%，創下自 2020 年以來的最高紀錄。這項數據顯示，在比特幣價格大幅下跌的背景下，長期持有者的活躍度正顯著攀升，可能為市場帶來潛在的拋售壓力。
（前情提要：比特幣回檔6.3萬、以太坊跌破1880！全網爆倉6.1億鎂，恐慌指數續走低）
（背景補充：美債規模飆至 39.7 兆美元創歷史新高！「貶值交易」遭引爆投資人瘋搶比特幣與黃金）
隨著比特幣（BTC）近期價格經歷顯著下殺，市場的避險情緒與恐慌指數隨之波動。台北時間 7 月 28 日，曾多次被權威外媒《彭博》（Bloomberg）引用的 CryptoQuant 認證作者 Darkfost，於 X（前 Twitter）發布了最新的鏈上數據分析，揭示了比特幣長期投資者的不尋常舉動。
💥 BTC exchange inflows from LTH recently hit a peak.
These inflows are shown in this chart as the percentage share that LTH inflows (90-dma) represent compared to the total share, which includes STH.
👉 Today 5.1% of exchange inflows belong to LTH. It’s almost a record, only… pic.twitter.com/enYA79tD0c
— Darkfost (@Darkfost_Coc) July 28, 2026
LTH 交易所流入佔比達 5.1%，逼近歷史高點
根據 Darkfost 分享的圖表分析，這項指標衡量的是長期持有者（LTH）的交易所流入量（以 90 日移動平均線計算）在總流入量（包含短期持有者 STH）中所佔的百分比份額。
他明確指出：「目前約有 5.1% 的交易所流入量是來自 LTH。這幾乎創下了歷史紀錄，只有在 2020 年時曾達到接近 5.5% 的更高水準。」將長期累積的資產轉移至交易所，通常被市場視為潛在的拋售意願或重新配置資產的準備動作。
大跌引發巨鯨活躍，趨勢有望近期平緩
Darkfost 強調，這種長期持有者資金大量流入交易所的動態，正巧發生在比特幣價格面臨大幅下跌的背景之下。
不過，他也為投資人打了一劑強心針。由於該數據指標採用的是 90 日移動平均線（90-dma），因此走勢的變化具備一定的延遲與慣性。Darkfost 預測，這個極端上升的趨勢很有可能會在不久後平緩下來；但無可否認的是，這項數據已經充分顯示出，那些通常被視為市場穩定力量的長期持有者們，在近期的劇烈波動中顯得相當活躍。

summary:
全球最知名的迷因柴犬「Doge（Kabosu）」飼主佐藤敦子（Atsuko Sato）近日緊急發布聲明，強烈否 […]

〈$CATE 是假幣！狗狗幣 Doge 主人怒斥「貓咪照遭盜用」，重申僅授權 Own The Doge 專案〉這篇文章最早發佈於動區BlockTempo《動區動趨-最具影響力的區塊鏈新聞媒體》。
full_text:
全球最知名的迷因柴犬「Doge（Kabosu）」飼主佐藤敦子（Atsuko Sato）近日緊急發布聲明，強烈否認與近期在社群上流傳的「$CATE」代幣有任何關聯。她嚴厲譴責該項目未經授權盜用其 Instagram 的貓咪照片來發行偽代幣，並重申目前她唯一官方合作且授權智慧財產權的加密專案，僅有「Own The Doge」以及其所推出的 $DOG 與 $COCORO 代幣。
（前情提要：馬斯克：明年也許讓「狗狗幣登上月球」，但DOGE幣價沒反應）
（背景補充：比特幣上9萬鎂，為何迷因幣 PEPE 與 DOGE 總在上漲時當前鋒？）
在加密貨幣市場中，迷因幣（Meme coin）的炒作往往伴隨著極高的熱度與風險，而知名 IP 遭不肖人士盜用的事件更是層出不窮。台北時間 7 月 28 日，全球最著名迷因柴犬 Kabosu（即 Doge 本尊）的飼主佐藤敦子（Atsuko Sato）透過 X（前 Twitter）官方帳號 @kabosumama 發布嚴正聲明，親自下場打假近期在市場上流傳的新迷因代幣。
先日、一連の $CATE トークンが、あたかも私と関係があるかのように広まりましたが、私はこれらのトークンとは一切関係ありません。
Instagramで猫について投稿した直後、その投稿が無断で利用され、偽のトークンが作られてしまいました。…
— かぼすママ (@kabosumama) July 28, 2026
愛貓照片遭盜用發幣，痛批百萬大 V 推廣
近期一個名為 $CATE 的代幣在社群網路上被廣泛宣傳，甚至被塑造成與 Kabosu 家族有關的官方項目。對此，佐藤敦子明確表示：「我與這些代幣完全沒有任何關係。」
她進一步揭露了該假幣的起源，指出自己日前剛在 Instagram 上發布關於家中愛貓的貼文，不久後，這些照片便遭到有心人士未經授權的惡意盜用，並以此為噱頭製作出了 $CATE 偽代幣。佐藤敦子對此感到非常遺憾與痛心，她特別提到，在這波惡意炒作中，甚至包含了一些在 X 平台上擁有龐大影響力與粉絲數的知名帳號，這些帳號的推波助瀾無疑加劇了社群的誤解與投資風險。
唯一官方認證：Own The Doge 與 $DOG、$COCORO
為了避免粉絲與投資人持續受騙，佐藤敦子在貼文中也清楚釐清了她目前在區塊鏈與加密貨幣領域的真實合作關係。她強調，關於她所有相關的智慧財產權（IP），她正式參與且授權的專案「只有 @OwnTheDoge」。
回顧合作歷史，Own The Doge 專案早於 2021 年便取得了 Doge NFT 的所有權，並隨後順利推出了 $DOG 代幣。該團隊不僅協助舉辦了知名的 Doge Day 活動，還積極支持各項慈善事業，並全權負責管理 Kabosu 的相關智慧財產權。此外，佐藤敦子也證實，在 2025 年時，雙方更進一步深化合作，於 Base 網路上共同推出了名為 $COCORO 的新代幣。
收益全數用於動物保護，呼籲社群保持警惕
作為一名深愛動物的飼主，佐藤敦子表示，透過與 Own The Doge 官方專案合作所獲得的所有收益，都已妥善運用於支持她身邊這些重要的「動物家人」的生活起居；同時，這些資金也透過 @withkabosu 帳號，實質投入並贊助了更廣泛的動物保護慈善活動。
在聲明的最後，佐藤敦子向廣大社群發出強烈呼籲，請大眾務必僅信任來自官方管道發布的公告資訊，並對於任何企圖蹭熱度、與她毫無關聯的來路不明專案或代幣保持高度警惕，以免成為不肖詐騙份子眼中的肥羊。

title: Mother and boyfriend guilty of murder of girl, two
summary: Prosecutors say Isabelle Welsh was subjected to a "wicked" campaign of abuse before her death.
full_text:
Mother and boyfriend guilty of murder of girl, two
- Published
Warning: This story contains distressing details
A mother and her new boyfriend have been found guilty of murdering her two-year-old daughter, with the man also convicted of sexually abusing the girl.
Isabelle Welsh suffered multiple injuries in the weeks before she collapsed with a fractured skull at her home in Thornaby in September 2025, Teesside Crown Court had heard.
Alexandra Walker, 25, and her partner Harrison Simpson, 22, were both found guilty of murder and child cruelty, with Simpson also convicted of sexual abuse of a child.
They will be sentenced on Thursday. Isabelle's family said she had her "whole life ahead of her" but it was "taken in the most heartbreaking way".
Prosecutors previously said the couple, who began a relationship in June 2025, were both responsible for a "wicked" campaign of sexual abuse and violence against Isabelle.
Walker and Simpson blamed each other for the girl's injuries and suffering.
Isabelle suffered her fatal injuries on the morning of 13 September while alone with Simpson, when Walker was upstairs in bed following a drink and drugs binge, the court heard.
Walker called 999 later that afternoon to say her daughter had collapsed at their home, with the two-year-old dying in hospital the following day.
The previously "happy and mischievous" girl was found to have a fractured skull and catastrophic brain injury, with doctors also discovering she was covered in bruises and suffered 21 broken bones in the weeks before her death.
Prosecutors said Isabelle's abuse started shortly after Simpson arrived in her life, with the extent of her injuries so obvious her mother must have known what was going on.
They said Walker prioritised her new relationship over the safety of her daughter, allowing Simpson to spend time alone with Isabelle despite suspecting he was a paedophile.
Simpson claimed he had no motive for harming Isabelle, while Walker said she did not hurt her daughter and was unaware of any abuse.
Jurors reached their verdicts after about six and a half hours of deliberation.
Simpson was unanimously found guilty of murder, cruelty and sexual assault of a child.
Walker was convicted of murder by a majority of 11 jurors to one and of cruelty unanimously.
She was found not guilty of sexually assaulting her daughter.
Ms Justice Norton said each murderer would get a life sentence, with the minimum term they would have to serve before being eligible for parole to be set by her on Thursday.
The judge thanked jurors for their work in the upsetting and distressing case.
'Robbed of her future'
In a statement released after the verdicts, Isabelle's family said: "Isabelle should have had her whole life ahead of her, but she was taken from us in the most heartbreaking way.
"She was so loved and our lives will never be the same without her.
"While today's verdicts cannot undo the pain caused or bring Isabelle back, it does mean justice has been served.
"We will remember Isabelle forever."
Det Ch Insp Steve Chatterton said Isabelle suffered "catastrophic injuries at the hands of the very people who should have loved, cared for and protected her".
Walker and Simpson "robbed Isabelle of her future" and "deprived her family of watching her grow up and achieve those milestones that so many take for granted", he added.
District crown prosecutor for the Crown Prosecution Service Kirstie Devine said Isabelle suffered "shocking violence" and "appalling abuse".
The "raft of evidence", which included phone records, CCTV and medical reports, showed "only the two adults who were regularly with Isabelle could have harmed her", she said.

title: House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly line-up
summary: She plays Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel, and  is the ninth celebrity to be confirmed.
full_text:
House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia joins Strictly line-up
- Published
House of the Dragon star Bethany Antonia is the latest celebrity to join this year's line-up for Strictly Come Dancing.
Antonia has portrayed dragon-rider Lady Baela Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones prequel since 2022. She is currently starring as Eurydice in the Tony Award-winning musical Hadestown in London's West End.
The singer and actress has also appeared in series including Nolly, Stay Close, Stath Lets Flats, and Doctor Who.
In a statement, Antonia said: "I can't quite believe that I will be heading to the Strictly ballroom this September! I have grown up watching Strictly, and I am so excited to take the challenge on and (hopefully!) learn a new skill. See you on the dancefloor!"
She is the ninth celebrity to be confirmed for this year's series, joining stars including Delta Goodrem, Lacey Turner, Dani Dyer and Jaime Winstone.
More celebrities are set to be announced in the coming weeks, with 15 expected in the final line-up.
Scroll down to see the rest of this year's line-up so far:
Jaime Winstone
Jaime Winstone launched her acting career in 2004 and her film credits include Bullet Boy, Tomb Raider and Wild Bill, as well stage productions such as 2:22 A Ghost Story.
The actress, who also won acclaim for her portrayal of Barbara Windsor in the BBC biopic Babs, said she was "so excited" to be joining the dance competition.
The actress said in a statement she was "no stranger to a dance floor", but added that ballroom is "a whole new world for me".
"I love a challenge though," she continued, "so can't wait to enter my showgirl era and get super sparkly!"
Winstone has also appeared in TV series such as Poirot, Dead Set, Torvill & Dean, Mad Dogs, Count Abdulla and Four Lives.
After playing Windsor in Babs, Winstone stepped into the late actress's famous role of Peggy Mitchell in EastEnders, appearing in flashback specials, most recently in the soap's 40th anniversary last year.
Dame Sarah Storey
Known as Great Britain's most successful Paralympian of all time, Dame Sarah Storey has secured 19 gold medals across the nine Paralympic Games she competed in.
The swimmer and cyclist said embarking on the challenge is "hugely exciting" and she "can't wait to get started".
"I have always loved watching Strictly and my daughter Louisa is a very talented dancer, so to be able to learn from the best and hopefully understand even more about her world, is incredibly motivating!" she said.
The former athlete won four golds at London 2012. She started her career as a swimmer and later switched to cycling, winning 30 Paralympic medals in total.
Will Best
Best is known for hosting Big Brother with AJ Odudu on ITV since 2023, and as host of the Hits Radio Breakfast Show alongside Fleur East and James Barr.
He said it was "an absolute dream" to be taking to the BBC One contest's dance floor in September, "albeit a pretty terrifying one".
Best added: "I've been lucky to do lots of live telly before, but absolutely nothing like this. And I cannot wait!
"I have no idea if I can actually dance, but bring on the sequins, bring on the quicksteps, bring on the dance floor! I'm going to try to enjoy every minute of it."
Cach Mercer
Mercer was part of the winning couple on ITV dating show Love Island last year, and also works as a model and DJ, and is an ambassador for a young people's mental health charity.
"I have grown up watching the show with my family and am so excited to now be part of the cast," he said.
Mercer also showcases his Afrobeat, hip-hop and street dance moves on his social media accounts.
"Dancing is a huge passion of mine and I can't wait to learn ballroom and do the foxtrot for the first time!" he added.
Delta Goodrem
Delta Goodrem is also part of this year's celebrity list, with the Australian singer and actress becoming the third celebrity to be announced for the upcoming series.
"I've been incredibly honoured to perform on many different stages throughout my career - from TV, theatre, film sets, to touring my own shows around the world," Goodrem said.
"There is, however, one stage I've never stepped onto and that is the ballroom floor. I'm absolutely thrilled to be joining Strictly and can't wait to get started."
She rose to fame in hit Australian soap opera Neighbours and recently represented her nation in the 2026 edition of the Eurovision Song Contest.
Chris Appleton
Celebrity hair stylist Chris Appleton is also part of this year's line-up.
Appleton, best known for his work with Kim Kardashian, joins singer-songwriter Delta Goodrem, EastEnders actress Lacey Turner and reality star Dani Dyer in the battle for the Glitterball trophy.
The Leicester-born Color Wow creative director said: "I'm thrilled to be joining Strictly Come Dancing and coming home to the UK for this incredible experience."
He has also created red carpet looks for the likes of Jennifer Lopez, Katy Perry and Ariana Grande, while having his work showcased on the covers of publications including Vogue, Harper's Bazaar and Vanity Fair.
"I've always believed that the best things happen when you take a chance and try something new," added the 43-year-old, who this year released a memoir entitled Your Roots Don't Define You.
"I may know my way around a salon floor, but the dance floor is a whole different story - and I can't wait to get started."
Lacey Turner
Lacey Turner was the first contestant to be announced for this year's series, which is expected to begin in September.
She said she was "so excited to be making my way to the dance floor", adding that she was a "huge fan" of the show.
Turner, 38, is best known for her role as Stacey Slater on the BBC One soap, which she joined in 2004.
She has won a British Soap Award and National Television Award for her role, and has also starred in TV dramas including the BBC's Our Girl.
In a video posted on Instagram, Turner said she was "so excited and so terrified at the same time" to be taking part in the show.
"But I've had so many friends do Strictly, and I thought it was about time that I pluck up the courage and made my way on to the dance floor."
Dani Dyer
Dani Dyer, the media personality and daughter of actor Danny Dyer appeared in the launch episode last year, but was then injured in training and pulled out before the competition began.
That incident has not put her off trying again. "I am so excited to be back in the ballroom this September," she said.
"I just cannot wait to get my dancing shoes back on and hopefully this time around I can actually make it to week one! I'm just over the moon and cannot wait to find out who else is doing it."
The 29-year-old, who first found fame on Love Island in 2018, fractured her ankle when she "landed funny" in rehearsals with dance partner Nikita Kuzmin before the competitive episodes began last September.
She was replaced by actress Amber Davies, another former Love Island winner, who went on to reach the Strictly final.
Earlier this year, Dyer was joint winner of Channel 4's Celebrity SAS: Who Dares Wins, and appeared with her dad in TV show The Dyers' Caravan Park.
Josh Widdicombe, Emma Willis and Johannes Radebe will take over as Strictly presenters this year, following the departures of Tess Daly and Claudia Winkleman.
The first line-up announcements were made significantly earlier than usual - the BBC usually confirms the line-up in August.
Speaking to ITV's Good Morning Britain in June, Ballas said: "There are going to be some people on there that will make you go 'wow'."
Asked about the new presenting trio, Ballas said she was "very excited to see what they bring" to the show.
"I know they took lots of chemistry tests, as did everybody, and those chemistry tests have brought those three people together, and I believe it's absolutely unbelievable," she said.
Ballas described the number of new elements on this year's show as "quite extraordinary", but added that it will still feel familiar to viewers.

title: 'It's a hell of a situation': Spain grapples with destructive wildfires
summary: Three fires in the Madrid region have caused special concerns, with a new heatwave expected to hit Spain from Wednesday.
full_text:
'It's a hell of a situation': Spain grapples with devastating wildfires
- Published
For the past week, firefighters have been tackling a series of wildfires ravaging the Spanish countryside, threatening dozens of communities and forcing more than 70,000 people to evacuate their homes.
Three fires in the Madrid region have caused special concerns, with a new heatwave expected to hit Spain from Wednesday, fuelling fears that firefighting efforts could be hindered.
"It's a hell of a situation," said Madrid regional leader Isabel Díaz Ayuso, as she visited affected areas on Monday alongside Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez.
Sánchez spoke on Tuesday of highly challenging hours and days ahead but of light beginning to appear "at the end of the tunnel".
Temperatures are expected to approach 40C in some regions in the coming days, with the heatwave forecast to last at least until Sunday.
Spain's state meteorological agency Aemet has warned the "fire danger level will continue to rise to extreme levels, hindering firefighting efforts".
Ayuso confirmed that four municipalities remained under lockdown orders while another 12 were evacuated. She had earlier described the wildfires as "the biggest natural catastrophe in the history of Spain" and of flames turning the area into a "war zone".
In the Madrid region alone, more than 56,500 people have been evacuated since the fires broke out last week. A further 27,797 people have been ordered to stay at home.
Further evacuations have taken place in Ávila, Toledo and Valencia.
Ayuso wrote on X that the situation was now "improving little by little" and some residents may soon be allowed to return home.
Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska told Spain's La 1 TV channel that firefighting efforts on Monday night had resulted in "relatively positive progress".
"This morning, we are very satisfied with the work done. We are going to consolidate the work that has been done," he said.
He maintained that "we must be positive; we have the emergency under control" but conceded that "weather conditions are not helping us at all".
Pedro Sánchez announced on Tuesday that areas affected by the wildfires have been declared "disaster zones".
"The climate emergency is worsening year after year, and we are required to be united to fight against fire, as well as in prevention and reconstruction," he told reporters during a briefing in Madrid.
"Therefore, I make an explicit request, a single appeal to all regional governments: Climate denial is the worst fuel for the fight against the climate emergency."
Spanish journalist Juan Navarro, who is in Cebreros - a town around 40 miles west of Madrid – told the BBC that people were looking with fear to the next heatwave.
When you drive through villages in the area around Cebreros, "everything is black", he said.
Ahead of the latest meeting of the Integrated Operational Coordination Centre (Cecopi), the mayors of two of the evacuated towns in the Madrid region described the fire as "a kitten by night and a lion by day".
Robledo de Chavela mayor Fernando Casado said his community would continue fighting "with their knives out".
Echoing his sentiments, Valdemaqueda mayor Ricardo Meneses added that "we can't let our guard down and we're on high alert because now is the time to stop the fire".
A psychologist visiting shelters has told El Mundo there is a growing sense of anxiety among the evacuees.
"We've seen cases of people who come in relatively relaxed on the first day because they think this situation might only last a day," said Sara Casado, of the Citizen Services Department of the Madrid region.
"But then they see how the hours and days go by. That uncertainty of being here without knowing when they'll be able to return increases their anxiety."
The Madrid region is currently under a red weather warning, with temperatures expected to reach 35C in mountainous areas and 38C in other parts of the community.
In its latest update, the national government's delegation in Madrid said the fire "remains active and uncontrolled".
"Today's efforts will focus on surveillance and cooling the affected areas in anticipation of the forecast worsening of weather conditions," it added.
Around 77,000 hectares (190,000 acres) have been affected by the fires in Spain, according to the minister for ecological transition, Sara Aagesen.
The wildfire burning in the Ávila area was the largest in the country's recent history, she added.
In Ávila, where more than 50,000 hectares have burned down since the start of the wildfires, the government's representative said the fire had a "quite favourable" evolution overnight.
Nicanor Sen, however, said there had been "small flare-ups" that were now being monitored by emergency services.
Meanwhile, the government of Valencia lifted a lockdown order for the town of Vall D'Uixo after a fire broke out of 25 July, forcing some 16,000 from 20 municipalities to evacuate.
In neighbouring Portugal, firefighters are tackling a large fire on three active fronts in the eastern Guarda area.

title: Gironde wildfires pick up as French region braces for new 40C heatwave
summary: Firefighters are braced for a sharp rise in temperatures on Wednesday, which could complicate the containment of wildfires.
full_text:
Gironde wildfires pick up as French region braces for new 40C heatwave
- Published
Firefighters in France are working around the clock to contain wildfires that have been raging in the Gironde region, while bracing for another sharp rise in temperatures.
"The fire is like David against Goliath," said Eric Brocardi, spokesman of the national firefighters' federation.
Four of his colleagues had died in recent weeks across France, he said, and 2,000 had been deployed in the Gironde to contain the flames, which for days have ravaged the countryside between the coastline and Bordeaux.
"Weather conditions were unfavourable," a local official warned, as this summer's fourth heatwave was expected to start by Wednesday, bringing temperatures in the area to 40C.
Bordeaux, which has a population of 260,000, is not currently under threat, according to officials.
But Commander Rémi Lassoureille, who is leading the firefighting response in the Gironde region, is worried about the western edge of the wildfire.
"We are frightened about the impact on Bordeaux and the metropolitan area," he said.
One of the wildfires burning on Monday was 15km (9 miles) from the periphery of Bordeaux, where the air quality has deteriorated dramatically in recent days.
"By Sunday evening everything had really begun to empty out," a holidaymaker from Essex told the BBC, adding that the air was "really smoky" with bits of ash. "People were staying indoors, so it was eerie, and very sad."
The majority of residents and tourists were wearing masks and the smell of smoke clung on to clothes for days, she said.
A firefighter "got a round of applause" as he walked through the Marché Chartrons square in Bordeaux where restaurants were having to close their doors because of the ash in the air, she added.
"The city has been very quiet," said Graham White, president of the Bordeaux British Community. "The shops, restaurants and cafes are fairly empty... Interestingly on Sunday when there was still smoke, there were people brave enough to sit outside on terraces."
White, who has been living in the area for several years, said this sort of event had not occurred before and was "something significant".
But some news reports had suggested the situation in Bordeaux was "akin to being the next Great Fire of London", which was not the case, White added.
President Emmanuel Macron, who visited the fire-ravaged area in the Gironde region on Monday, said the country was facing a "completely unprecedented wildfire... the "toughest since World War Two".
Health Minister Stéphanie Rist said the government was being "very vigilant" in terms of air pollution and urged people in the affected areas to stay indoors.
On Tuesday morning the Gironde prefect ordered a new evacuation of all camping sites near the coast at Lacanau, while those in the nearby town were allowed to stay put but told to prepare for sudden evacuation.
About 4,000 tourists told to leave the area are in addition to the 220,000 people evacuated around France in recent days.
An estimated 240 homes and houses have been destroyed, officials have said.
By midday on Tuesday firefighters were already intervening in various parts of the region to tackle fires that were picking up again.
A 23-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of starting a fire in the Var region. He faces 15 years' imprisonment.
Peggy Plouhinec, the general director of Château Picque Caillou - one of the few wine estates on the west side of Bordeaux - told the BBC that her business chose to close at the weekend because of the smoke, but that the situation had improved since then and that a bout of rain on Sunday night had helped.
While her vineyards were not at risk, she said tourists had "deserted" the region. "The hospitality sector will be impacted this summer, that's for sure," she added. "What is happening is unprecedented. We're lucky that we haven't been too affected yet, but the business will still suffer from the lower numbers of tourists."
"But many people have lost their homes or their businesses, not to mention the firefighters who have been hard at work for weeks now and who must be exhausted."
One resident of Cap Ferret, which was evacuated late last week, told French media that his main concern now was for the peninsula he lived in, rather than the big city city inland.
"Everyone talks about saving Bordeaux, but in Bordeaux there's nothing but concrete. Have you ever seen concrete burn?"
"Here, there are only trees... and when you see all that has burned, it's a catastrophe."
Additional reporting by Xavier Pallas

title: Can Burnham's vision for Manchester's schools really work for the rest of England?
summary: The prime minister's plans for technical education have their roots in the Manchester Baccalaureate.
full_text:
Can Burnham's vision for Manchester's schools really work for the rest of England?
- Published
Two years ago, I stood at the back of a conference room in Manchester Hall, sipping a coffee and watching Andy Burnham unveil his vision for transforming technical education in Greater Manchester.
He had announced plans for the Manchester Baccalaureate, or MBacc, the year before, and, armed with PowerPoint slides and guest speakers, was running through the ins and outs in front of a room full of education and business leaders.
Now, as prime minister, Burnham has announced plans to make that idea national, and overhaul the technical education system across the whole of England.
The details are still scarce at this stage. We know it will involve giving pupils the option to study more vocational courses and take up work experience from Year 10, but how it will work in practice is still up in the air.
One thing that is certain is that the thinking behind it, and the ambition, is the same as that which underpins the MBacc: a determination to give teenagers a clear, step-by-step route into more practical and technical jobs.
The trouble is, the MBacc itself can be quite a difficult concept to get your head around if you're not familiar with it.
Let's be clear from the start: it's not another type of qualification, like the T-levels and V-levels announced in England in recent years.
Instead, it's a framework that aims to give teenagers a "clear line of sight to good jobs" in vocational and technical areas.
The best way to think about it is a step-by-step route - picture a flow chart - that teenagers can follow from school into any given technical career.
It's set up in parallel to a more clearly defined academic route. During that conference event in July 2024, Burnham and other speakers made clear that those who want to go on to desk jobs can follow a well-trodden path of GCSEs, A-levels, and a university degree.
But for those who want more practical careers, the landscape is much more complicated.
The MBacc is best seen as an effort to simplify that landscape, spelling out for teenagers who want to go into more vocational or technical careers which courses they can study, and ensuring they have the opportunity to study them along with hands-on work experience.
It spells out routes to careers in seven different categories:
- Construction and the green economy 
- Creative, culture and sport 
- Digital and technology 
- Education and early years 
- Financial, business and professional services 
- Health and social care 
- Manufacturing and engineering 
Its success is difficult to measure, since the MBacc is still in its infancy.
It's not until 2030 that it seeks to achieve its mission of guaranteeing every young person a clear path to good jobs. By 2035, the aim is for every young person to have 45 days of work experience by the time they're 19.
According to the most recent data, the MBacc has been rolled out across 101 secondary schools and colleges in Greater Manchester - about 40% of the total.
The Greater Manchester Combined Authority says 1,405 young people accessed workplace experiences during its second year.
Time will tell, as those teenagers leave school and enter the world of work, how transformative it will be.
And what works in Greater Manchester may not work everywhere else.
The prime minister has stated explicitly that he wants to expand the approach across England.
"I created the Greater Manchester Baccalaureate or MBacc... to bridge the gap between our schools and our employers," he wrote in the Times. "Now we're taking that idea national."
It may well be scalable. The seven MBacc "gateways" - although designed specifically around Greater Manchester's "fastest-growing industries" - are actually quite broad-ranging. They mirror some of the areas already targeted by efforts to boost technical education at a national level. There are T-levels in construction areas as well as in education and early years, for example.
But there will be challenges along the way.
The prime minister is clear that he wants technical and vocational education to be tied to local economies. He plans to work with local leaders, employers and schools, to "identify the industries driving growth in local areas and make sure that local kids have a clear route into them".
If that's to be the case, he will need to make sure that teenagers in all parts of England - including in areas without thriving industries - don't fall through the gaps.

title: Booker Prize longlist: See the 13 'dynamite' novels up for this year's prestigious award
summary: Elizabeth Strout, Douglas Stuart and Marlon James are among the 13 authors recognised this year.
full_text:
Booker Prize longlist: See the 13 'dynamite' novels up for this year's prestigious award
- Published
Elizabeth Strout, Douglas Stuart, Marlon James and Rebecca Perry are among the authors who have been longlisted for this year's Booker Prize.
The 13 chosen books include novels set in Mexico City, a remote Scottish island, an assissted suicide clinic in Zurich, 1980s Jamaica, and Massachussetts before the 2024 US election.
Chair of the judges Mary Beard described the 13 novels as "dynamite", adding: "We are confident that our longlist of books has something for everyone."
The longlist, referred to as the Booker Dozen, will be whittled down to a shortlist on 22 September, before the winner is announced on 9 November.
The annual Booker Prize is the literary world's most prestigious award, recognising long-form fiction by writers of any nationality, written in English and published in the UK or Ireland.
The six shortlisted authors will receive £2,500 each and a specially bound edition of their book, while the eventual winner will receive a trophy and £50,000 in prize money.
High-profile authors who missed this year's longlist include Maggie O'Farrell, Ann Patchett, John Lanchester, Deborah Levy and Julian Barnes, who many predicted would be recognised for his final book Departure(s).
Booker Prize 2026: The longlist in full
- The Shadow of the Object by Chloe Aridjis 
- Switzy by Emma Cline 
- Helen of Nowhere by Makenna Goodman 
- The End of Everything by M. John Harrison 
- The Disappearers by Marlon James 
- Black Bag by Luke Kennard 
- The Renovation by Kenan Orhan 
- May We Feed the King by Rebecca Perry 
- The Palm House by Gwendoline Riley 
- The Things We Never Say by Elizabeth Strout 
- John of John by Douglas Stuart 
- All Them Dogs by Djamel White 
- The Vivisectors by Missouri Williams 
The Booker judges received 163 submissions for this year's prize before settling on the final 13.
Each of the five judges read all the submitted books, with Beard joking she "occasionally felt daunted as a new box of 30 or so gleaming volumes landed on my doorstep".
"But what I shall most remember is the eye-opening pleasure of it all, and what I learnt about reading and the power of fiction from my fellow judges."
What are the longlisted books about?
Three of this year's authors in the Booker Dozen are previous shortlistees, including Elizabeth Strout, who is recognised for The Things We Never Say.
It follows a high school history teacher in Massachusetts who is grappling with isolation, post-pandemic social anxiety, and concern about the forthcoming 2024 US election.
The two other former shortlistees have also previously won the prize. Shuggie Bain author Douglas Stuart is recognised this time for John of John, about a young gay man who returns to his strict religious family on a remote Scottish island.
Another former winner, Marlon James, returns this year with The Disappearers, a 600-page book due to be released in September about eight gay men in Kingston, Jamaica, who are targeted by a violent mob during a play rehearsal.
James's is the longest book this year, while the shortest is Helen of Nowhere by Makenna Goodman - a 140-page novel which follows a disgraced professor touring an idyllic countryside house, learning about its previous owner.
Another longlistee, Rebecca Perry, won the Waterstones Debut Fiction Prize earlier this month for her novel May We Feed The King, about a curator of historic buildings who begins to explore the life of an almost-forgotten medieval king.
Two other authors are recognised for debut works - including Kenan Orhan for The Renovation, about a psychologist caring for her dementia-suffering father in Italy when some building work doesn't go to plan.
Fellow debut novelist Djamel White is recognised for All Them Dogs, which follows a man returning to west Dublin after being on the run for five years because he killed someone in a gang fight.
Aged 28, White is the youngest longlistee this year. The oldest is 81-year-old M John Harrison, for The End of Everything, a post-apocalyptic novel set in a Kent coastal town.
Switzy by Emma Cline, due to be published in September, is about a wealthy and accomplished man travelling to an assisted suicide clinic in Switzerland; while The Shadow of the Object by Chloe Aridjis sees an encounter in a Mexico City hospital lead to a life-changing friendship.
Gwendoline Riley's The Palm House, meanwhile, follows a London freelancer and her long friendship with a senior magazine editor; and Missouri Williams's The Vivisectors follows a graduate student in a decaying university city overrun by wild plants.
The list is completed by Luke Kennard's Black Bag, about a penniless out-of-work actor who is paid to zip himself inside a large black leather bag and sit silently at the back of a university lecture hall for a psychological experiment.
In a statement, Beard said: "Every writer on our longlist brilliantly musters the power of words on the page to take the reader to new places, to see old places from new angles, to change minds.
"Books are not mirrors: they don't simply reflect ourselves back to us. One of the many important things about fiction is that it helps us see what it might be like not to be us, to begin to understand the perspectives of others, and to imagine what it might be like to see the world differently.
"Great books are not cosy. In their various ways, the novels we have chosen are (we hope) dynamite."
Last year's Booker Prize was won by British-Hungarian author David Szalay, for his novel Flesh.

title: Search begins for King's new top aide
summary: The King will need a new private secretary, with Sir Clive Alderton stepping down next year.
full_text:
Search begins for King's new top aide
- Published
The search will soon begin for a new right-hand man or woman for King Charles, with the current principal private secretary, Sir Clive Alderton, set to step down next year.
This highly influential, behind the scenes, figure is responsible for organising the King and Queen's official work, advising on events such as the Coronation and also getting involved in more personal aspects of the monarchy.
Sir Clive was there to give a formal welcome to Andy Burnham last week when he arrived at Buckingham Palace to become the new prime minister.
Meanwhile the Duke of Sussex dubbed him "the Wasp" in his memoir, as he described the private secretary's role in discussions about Prince Harry and the Duchess of Sussex stepping down as working royals and moving to the US.
Sir Clive, who joined the Royal Household 20 years ago, will stay in post until his 60th birthday in May 2027, with a Palace source saying he would help with the handover to his successor, once he or she has been appointed.
A Palace spokesman said the King and Queen were "deeply grateful to Sir Clive for his tireless support and wise counsel over the years, and for the enduring loyalty that will ensure a smooth transition to his successor".
Sir Clive was a familiar sight accompanying the King and Queen on visits and state occasions - and he had helped them with a smooth transition when they had taken to the throne in September 2022.
The outgoing principal private secretary had an annual pay package of £300,000 to £305,000.
A former diplomat, Sir Clive's backroom position in the Palace was similar to a permanent secretary in Whitehall, not front of stage, but with much hidden influence and access to power, as they advised and helped to put plans into action.
Prince Harry, who talked about a number of courtiers in less than flattering terms in his book Spare, described the influential role of a figure he called "the Wasp", who was widely seen as Sir Clive.
This involved playing a part in plans for the Duke and Duchess of Sussex's changed role and their departure from the UK in 2020.
As well as being a gatekeeper and chief adviser to the monarch, Sir Clive also referenced the importance of having a sense of humour, on a job that might go from meeting President Donald Trump to a local visit and a state occasion.
"It has been the greatest imaginable honour to serve the King and Queen in my present role through such historic times and with unforgettable humour along the way," said Sir Clive.

title: Richard Hammond fined £999 for  speeding offences
summary: The TV host is caught speeding twice in Herefordshire in the space of three weeks, magistrates hear.
full_text:
Richard Hammond fined £999 for speeding offences
- Published
Former Top Gear presenter Richard Hammond has been fined £999 after being caught speeding twice in three weeks while driving luxury cars.
The 56-year-old was captured driving his Porsche Taycan Cross Turismo at 68mph in a 50mph limit on the A40 in Pencraig, Herefordshire on 2 December.
He was later clocked driving his Bentley Continental GT at 82mph in a 70mph limit on the A50 Rudhall Overbridge, also in Herefordshire, on 22 December.
Hammond pleaded guilty to two speeding charges through his solicitor. Two further charges that he had ignored the police letters and failed to identify himself as the guilty driver were withdrawn by police.
He was also given seven penalty points for his licence at the hearing last week.
Magistrate Ann Minton ordered him to pay a total of £1,771, comprising two fines of £333 and £666, £240 in costs and victim surcharges totalling £532.
Documents from the case case show Hammond was first caught speeding by a police officer with a handheld speed camera at just before 13:00 BST on 2 December and again at about 11:45 BST on 22 December.
West Mercia Police sent speeding tickets to a Grade II listed Herefordshire castle bought by Hammond in 2012 and a £1m farm estate near Hereford, but the letters were returned marked as "addressee gone away".
He was eventually tracked down to his £2m home near Abergavenny in Wales where more than 30 vehicles were currently registered, the court heard.
Police also set out in the court papers that Hammond had been accused of another driving offence in August last year.
Hammond, who hosted the BBC's Top Gear show with Jeremy Clarkson and James May between 2002 and 2015, received a three-month driving ban in France in 2013 after he and Clarkson were caught speeding while making an episode of the show.
To the charges of ignoring the police letters and failing to identify himself as the guilty driver, he said in a letter to the court read out by his solicitor: "He replied identifying himself as the driver. He sent the reply by First Class post. He posted the reply himself."
The force ultimately opted to withdraw the extra charges, as Hammond was prosecuted and convicted for the speeding.

Former boxing world champion denies assaulting man, court hears
